main_text.p: de vite, & ficut (folium) marcescit de ficu.

Quoniam inebriatus est in coelis gladius meus:& ecce descendet super Ædom,& super populum qui est in anathemate meo, in judicium. Gladius Domini impletus est sanguine, impinguatus est ab adipe, de sanguine agnorum & hircorum : de adipe re-num arietum : quoniam vistimam[?] (habet) Dominus in Bozra, & mactationem magnam in terra Ædom. Descendentq; uni-cornes cum eis, & tauri cum magnificis, & inebriabitur terra eorum a sanguine,& pulvis eorum ab adipe impinguabitur. Est enim dies ultionis Domini, annus retributionū[?] pro judicio Zion. Et convertentur flumina eius in pice,& pulvis eius in sulphur: eritq; terra eius in picem ardentem. Noctu & interdiu non extinguetur,in seculu ascendet fumus eius, a generatione in generatione devastabitur: in perpetuis æternitatibus nemo transibit per eam. Sed accipiet eam in possessionem pelicanus & ulula:noctua & corvus habitabunt in ea, extendetq; super eam funiculum inanem, & lapides per pendiculi vani. Nobiles eius vocabunt, & non erit ibi regnum:& cūcti principes eius erunt nihilum. Proferet (terra) in palatiis

page.notes: Page number "346" at the head is partly unclear (the first digit may be a 3 or a long-s form); marked [?]. "vistimam" reads as printed "uiftimam" with long s taken as s; the intended word is probably "victimam", so the reading is doubtful. "retributionu" may carry a tilde over the u; marked [?]. "cūcti" is read with a tilde over the u as printed. Running head "IESAIAE" converted to "JESAIAE" per the i/j rule. Hyphenated line-end words "re-num", "ma-gnam" and "uni-cornes" keep their printed hyphens; "sanguine", "super" and "pulvis" are written whole because their line-end breaks carry no printed hyphen.
